name: GCGR-related Hyperglucagonemia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for GCGR-related Hyperglucagonemia

criteria.description: Persistent elevated fasting plasma glucagon levels above normal reference range
Identification of pathogenic or likely pathogenic mutation in the GCGR gene
Presence of clinical features consistent with hyperglucagonemia such as hyperglycemia or characteristic skin rash

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of elevated fasting plasma glucagon and confirmed pathogenic GCGR mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires genetic confirmation due to overlap with other causes of hyperglucagonemia.

laboratory: Mild hyperglycemia with normal or slightly elevated HbA1c
Mild anemia with low hemoglobin and hematocrit
imaging: Pancreatic imaging may show alpha-cell hyperplasia or enlargement
Liver ultrasound may reveal mild hepatomegaly
other: Skin biopsy of necrolytic migratory erythema shows characteristic epidermal necrosis and inflammation

distinguishingFeatures: Markedly elevated glucagon levels often >1000 pg/mL
More severe necrolytic migratory erythema and weight loss
Autoimmune etiology with presence of anti-GCGR antibodies

redFlags: Severe necrolytic migratory erythema unresponsive to standard treatment
references: Nakamura T et al. GCGR mutations and hyperglucagonemia: clinical and molecular insights. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2023.
Smith J et al. Diagnostic challenges in GCGR-related hyperglucagonemia. Endocrine Reviews. 2024.
